title: Zotero Note Capture Lag
dataSources: Highlights (`reading:highlight`), book activity (`reading:book`), reviews (`reading:review`), paper libraries (`research:paper`), sync states (`reading:sync`).
app: Reading and second-brain telemetry — Readwise review exports, Kindle highlights, Goodreads shelves, and Zotero research libraries — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs, exports, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=research:paper collection=* first_opened_epoch=* first_note_epoch=*
| eval lag_days=round((first_note_epoch-first_opened_epoch)/86400,1)
| stats avg(lag_days) as avg_lag_days, max(lag_days) as worst_lag_days by collection
| sort - avg_lag_days
description: Measures note-capture lag by collection for paper-to-note workflows.
value: Lag tracking shows which collection create the slowest handoffs, syncs, or review loops inside paper-to-note workflows.
implementation: Capture the timestamps needed to compute `note-capture lag` on `research:paper` events and aggregate them by `collection`.
visualization: Table of collection with average and worst note-capture lag.
grandmaExplanation: It nudges how long things take for each collection so you can see where paper-to-note workflows slows down.
